summary: Generic key-value store keyed by (scope, key) that any Atlas application can use to persist user-facing UI state across page reloads and sessions.

classification.why_platform: PreferenceStore provides a reusable, domain-agnostic persistence primitive. It stores opaque JSON values without interpreting their meaning. Domain semantics and lifecycle rules belong to consuming applications. The component is technically generic: it uses a typed (scope, key) addressing scheme that any component can use without coupling.
non_goals: Preference schema validation or type enforcement
Interpretation or transformation of stored values

consumes: Shared Atlas Postgres instance (02_Platform/Postgres) — connection via ATLAS_PG_* environment variables
platform_contracts.contracts.Dataset — for all read endpoint responses (R-CON-BP-04)
platform_errorhandling — ApiError shape for error responses
provides: HTTP API: GET /preferences/{scope}/{key} — retrieve one preference or 404
HTTP API: PUT /preferences/{scope}/{key} — upsert a preference, returns 200
HTTP API: DELETE /preferences/{scope}/{key} — remove a preference, returns 204
HTTP API: GET /preferences/{scope} — retrieve all preferences for a scope as Dataset
HTTP API: GET /health — liveness check, returns {status: ok}
invariants: scope and key are always non-empty and contain no leading or trailing whitespace after validation
value_json is always valid JSON (enforced by JSONB column type)
PUT is always an upsert — no separate create/update distinction
updated_at is always set by the server (Postgres default now()) on every upsert
A GET on a (scope, key) that does not exist always returns 404 with ApiError
A DELETE on a (scope, key) that does not exist returns 204 (idempotent)
All read endpoints return Dataset per R-CON-BP-04
failure_modes: PREFERENCE_NOT_FOUND — GET on missing (scope, key) — 404 ApiError
INVALID_SCOPE — scope is empty or contains only whitespace — 422 ApiError
INVALID_KEY — key is empty or contains only whitespace — 422 ApiError
DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE — Postgres unreachable at startup or during request — 503 ApiError
INVALID_VALUE — PUT body missing 'value' field or malformed JSON — 422 ApiError

provides: PreferenceItem: {scope: str, key: str, value: Any, updated_at: datetime} — internal read model exposed via Dataset rows

consumes: psycopg2 connection pool — via 02_Platform/LabelEngine pattern (SimpleConnectionPool, RealDictCursor)
provides: GET /preferences/{scope}/{key} — returns Dataset with one row, or 404 ApiError
PUT /preferences/{scope}/{key} — body: {value: <any JSON>}, returns 200 with {scope, key, value, updated_at}
GET /preferences/{scope} — returns Dataset with all rows for scope; empty Dataset (rows=[]) if no preferences exist for scope

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /preferences/{scope}/{key}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Retrieve a single preference by scope and key. Returns Dataset (one row). Returns 404 ApiError if not found.

exposed_surfaces.name: PUT /preferences/{scope}/{key}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Create or overwrite a preference. Body: {value: <any JSON>}. Returns 200 with the stored record.

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /preferences/{scope}/{key}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Remove a preference. Idempotent — returns 204 whether or not the preference existed.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /preferences/{scope}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Retrieve all preferences for a scope. Returns Dataset. Empty rows list if no preferences exist for scope.

internal_flow.name: request_validation
internal_flow.description: FastAPI path parameter extraction. scope and key are validated: non-empty, no leading/trailing whitespace. If invalid, return 422 ApiError immediately.

internal_flow.name: connection_acquisition
internal_flow.description: Acquire a psycopg2 connection from the pool via context manager get_db(). If pool unavailable, raise causing 503.

internal_flow.name: database_operation
internal_flow.description: Execute the appropriate SQL: SELECT for GET, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE for PUT, DELETE for DELETE. All queries use parameterized statements.

internal_flow.name: response_construction
internal_flow.description: For GET endpoints: wrap result(s) in Dataset. For PUT: return stored record as typed response. For DELETE: return 204. For 404: return ApiError.

internal_required.role: Shared Postgres instance — PreferenceStore owns the 'preferences' schema within it
Dataset, DatasetMeta, ColumnSchema types for read endpoint responses

internal_optional.role: Structured logging, exception handlers, request timing — same optional import pattern as LabelEngine

forbidden: Domain-specific logic or validation of stored values

persistence.notes: PreferenceStore owns the 'preferences' schema in the shared Atlas Postgres instance. Schema is initialized idempotently at startup (CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).

platform_implementer: Implement app/database.py: connection pool init, schema init (inline DDL matching 10_schema.sql), get_db context manager — mirror LabelEngine pattern
Implement app/main.py: FastAPI app, CORS middleware (localhost only), optional platform_errorhandling import, on_startup hook calling init_pool and init_schema, health endpoint
Implement app/routers/preferences.py: all four endpoints with scope/key validation, Dataset construction, ApiError responses
Implement app/models.py: PutPreferenceRequest (body model), PreferenceRecord (response model for PUT)
Produce Dockerfile mirroring LabelEngine pattern (python:3.12-slim, /platform_packages, uvicorn CMD)
Produce compose.yml: service name 'preference-store', container name 'atlas-preference-store', port 127.0.0.1:8060:8000, ATLAS_PG_* env vars, atlas-net network
Produce pyproject.toml with project name 'preference_store' and same dependency set as LabelEngine
test_writer: GET /preferences/{scope}/{key} — existing key returns Dataset with one row containing correct value and updated_at
GET /preferences/{scope}/{key} — missing key returns 404 ApiError with code PREFERENCE_NOT_FOUND
PUT /preferences/{scope}/{key} — new key creates preference, returns 200 with stored record
PUT /preferences/{scope}/{key} — existing key overwrites value, updated_at advances
PUT /preferences/{scope}/{key} — value is null (valid JSON null) — stores successfully
PUT /preferences/{scope}/{key} — missing 'value' field in body — returns 422
DELETE /preferences/{scope}/{key} — existing key removes it, returns 204
GET /preferences/{scope} — scope with multiple preferences returns Dataset with all rows
GET /preferences/{scope} — scope with no preferences returns Dataset with empty rows list
scope validation — empty scope returns 422 with code INVALID_SCOPE
key validation — whitespace-only key returns 422 with code INVALID_KEY
reviewer: Verify Dataset is returned for both GET endpoints per R-CON-BP-04
Verify ApiError shape matches platform_errorhandling contract for all error responses
Verify DELETE is idempotent (204 on missing key)
Verify scope/key validation covers leading/trailing whitespace per definition

deferred_decisions: Port assignment for compose.yml — 8060 assumed; confirm no conflict with other platform services

risks.impact: If another component or future migration creates a 'preferences' schema, the idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS will silently mask conflicts. The DBA or migration tooling must be aware of schema ownership.
With no TTL or cleanup API, stale preferences from deprecated application features accumulate indefinitely. Operational cleanup requires direct DB access.

open_questions.question: Port 8060 for compose.yml — is this available or does it conflict with another Atlas platform service?
